diagram_recommendation: optional; a compact naturality pair can clarify the adjunction, but the explicit Hom bijection and inverse maps are already self-contained

checks.bijection_direction: Correct: alpha sends Hom_G(Ind_H^G W,V) to Hom_H(W,Res_H^G V); beta is its inverse.
checks.domains_and_codomain: alpha(Phi)(w)=Phi(eta_w), where eta_w is the function supported on H with eta_w(h)=h^{-1}w. beta(psi)(f)=sum_{t in T} t.psi(f(t)) lies in V, with T a left transversal for G/H.
checks.action_conventions: Consistent with f(gh)=h^{-1}f(g) and (x.f)(g)=f(x^{-1}g). For x^{-1}t=t'h, covariance and H-equivariance give t.psi(f(x^{-1}t))=x t'.psi(f(t')), so reindexing proves G-equivariance.
checks.coset_indexing: T indexes left cosets tH in G/H; the sum is finite since G is finite. No double-coset indexing occurs.
checks.tensor_balancing: Not applicable; no tensor product is used.
checks.inverse_checks: beta(psi)(eta_w)=psi(w), using e in T; and sum_t t.eta_{f(t)}=f, since at th its value is h^{-1}f(t)=f(th).
checks.naturality: The maps are natural in W contravariantly and V covariantly. For an H-map u:W'->W, u composed with eta_{w'} equals eta_{u(w')}, giving compatibility with precomposition by Ind(u) and by u. For a G-map v:V->V', postcomposition commutes with alpha and beta because v preserves the G-action and finite sums.
checks.rendering: Both listed screenshots were viewed at original resolution. The Hom statement and proof formulas are legible and typeset; no TikZ diagram is present in the capture. The second tile shows the proof's closing line.

suggested_diagram: If added, show the natural Hom bijection with separate naturality squares: for H-maps W'->W, precomposition on both Hom sets; for G-maps V->V', postcomposition on both Hom sets. Label alpha(Phi)(w)=Phi(eta_w) and beta(psi)(f)=sum_{t in T}t.psi(f(t)), with T representing G/H.
